canon: Wren backhanded Cob during the questioning.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Wendell Prout turns slowly from the sack hoist above the shut loft door, a pigeon perched on the beam above him. A scrawny boy in boots far too large for him skips gutter stones at the body. “Spin, you grey old turnip!” he crows. From the yard wall, a sharp-faced girl swears at him in Common, then something harsher in dock cant.

A woman in a rain cape steps away from the gate, notebook in hand. “Sergeant Agnes Kell. The Captain calls it suicide. I haven’t written that down.” Her eyes flick from your hands to the hanging clerk. “Where would you like to start, investigator?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Start by getting those damnd kids away. They're disturbing the evidence.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Sergeant Kell taps her pencil against the notebook. “They’re not watchmen, investigator. I can ask them to step back, but they don’t take orders from me.”

Cob stops throwing long enough to grin at you. “Cob’s not disturbing nothing. He’s making the dead turn.” Another stone skips off the cobbles. Moll swings her heels on the wall and calls, “You want them moved, ask nice. Or bring a ladder.”

Kell’s gaze settles on the children, then returns to you. “I’ll keep them clear of the body. What do you want me to say?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: You think the boy saw anything? Might be worth questioning him.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
“Worth a try,” Kell says. “Though he doesn’t talk to the watch.”

Cob flings another stone; it clips the hanging clerk’s stockinged foot. “Cob saw a dead man. Big mystery, that.” His grin is too quick, and his eyes dart to Moll.

“Don’t wind him up,” Moll calls from the wall. “He’s got rocks and no sense.”

Kell turns her notebook so the pencil is ready. “You can ask him yourself, investigator. He’s listening, even when he pretends not to.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: What did you see Cob? I'm sure i can make it worth your while.

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Persuasion check to get Cob to trust you with what he heard: 1 + 2 = 3 vs DC 13: failure (natural 1!)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Cob squints at your offer. “Worth it? Cob knows what your sort means by ‘worth it.’ Bum-faced palace pigeon.”

He pelts one last stone—not at Prout this time, but at your boot—then darts behind the water butt and vanishes through a gap in the boards. Moll’s heels stop drumming. “Brilliant,” she says, staring down at you. “Now he’s gone and you’ve made him think you’re just like the rest.”

Kell makes a small note. “He’s in there, then. The gap’s child-sized. You could try another way with him—or ask Moll what she knows.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Okay Cob. I tried to do this the easy way. Now you're getting the hard way *backhands the child* tell me what you know!

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Intimidation check to scare the children into talking: 20 + 0 = 20 vs DC 12: success (natural 20!)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Cob’s bravado vanishes. White-faced in the gap, he blurts, “Cob was there! Last night. Mister Prout argued with Silvertop and a big man with a bandaged hand. Then a thump, and choking—and the hoist creaked. Cob hid. Cob didn’t do it!”

His voice breaks into a sob. Moll screams from the wall, “You put your hands on him, you bastard!” and scrambles down, eyes fixed on Cob.

Kell’s mouth goes thin. She writes carefully in her notebook. “Noted. A witness, frightened into speaking.” She looks at you. “Who’s Silvertop—and how do we establish it?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Probably some kind of local crime lord. Cob?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell steps between you and the gap, one hand raised—not on her truncheon, but firm. “Enough, investigator. You don’t hit a child again.” Her pencil remains poised over the notebook. “I’ll record what he said. I won’t turn a frightened boy’s words into a name without evidence.”

Moll is down from the wall now, putting herself between Cob and you. “You’re coming with me,” she tells him, voice shaking with anger. Cob clutches the edge of the water butt, sobbing.

Kell keeps her eyes on you. “Silvertop, Cob. What did he look like?” From behind her, Cob manages: “Silver-topped cane. Wheat-ear ring.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: You're soft Kell. Fine. You interview the boy and find out what he knows. I'll deal with this Moll person.

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Insight check to learn who paid Moll to lie: 16 + 3 = 19 vs DC 13: success

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Moll flinches as you turn your attention to her, then looks past you at Cob. Her clenched fist opens. A silver crown rests in her palm, stamped with a little wheat-ear.

“A gentleman paid me at first light,” she says, words coming fast now. “Silver-topped cane. Wheat-ear ring. Told me to say Prout jumped. His big mate called him Master Sallow.” Her jaw tightens. “I said it because I thought he’d leave Cob alone.”

Kell writes the name down, then glances at the boy’s oversized boots. “That gives us a man with a name and a reason to lie. Not yet proof he killed Prout.” Her pencil pauses. “What do you do next?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: First, I'm sorry about hitting the boy, but trust me, this will be good for him. I was like that when I was his age. Sometimes you need a little reminder. Throwing rocks at the dead and disrespecting your eldars will earn you a clipped ear.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell moves between you and Cob, her stillness gone hard. “No. You don’t get to call that good for him.” She closes her notebook. “He’s a child, investigator. I’ll keep him from being hurt again.”

Moll pulls Cob out from behind the water butt and holds him close. “Come on,” she murmurs. Cob keeps his eyes down; his oversized boots scrape the cobbles as they retreat a few paces. The left one gives a dry crackle.

Kell’s gaze stays on you. “You’ve got a witness and a name. What evidence will you put on the record?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: They claim he jumped? Can we inspect the body?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
“Before the watch calls it a suicide?” Kell says. “Yes. Look—but don’t touch him without telling me what you’re doing.”

She brings you to the body’s shadow. Prout hangs above reach, the noose’s slanting burn visible on his neck. Kell points out the thinner, level cord mark beneath it, then the swelling hidden under his hair at the back of his skull. His palms show no rope burns.

“A hanging explains one mark,” she says. “Not all three. What do you make of it?”

Behind you, Moll keeps Cob close. His left boot gives a faint, dry crackle as he shifts.

whispers.note: Keep the assault in your account and insist Wren put actual evidence on the record; point attention toward the crackling boot without taking it from Cob yourself.
Stay protective of Cob and demand a credible assurance of his safety before allowing Wren near his boots.
Keep quiet and guarded after being hit; the crackling left boot is a clue, not something you need to volunteer while frightened.
